text: Below a certain depth, no fish has ever been found. Anywhere.
Eight thousand three hundred and thirty-six metres. In 2022, in a trench south of Japan, scientists filmed a snailfish there.
It's the deepest fish anyone has ever seen.
And it's right at the edge. Scientists think fish hit a wall at around eight thousand two hundred to eight thousand four hundred metres.
But the ocean doesn't stop there. It keeps going — for more than two and a half kilometres.
And the wall isn't the pressure crushing them.
So if it isn't the crush — what stops a fish?
The answer is level eleven of the full dive, linked right here.
